name: Global WAN - 4 cities + Cloud VPC, 2,000 IoT/scanners
topology: Hub-and-spoke WAN with cloud transit at hub

rationale.subject: Profile 'global_wan'
rationale.decision: Hub-and-spoke WAN with cloud transit at hub
rationale.justification: 4 cities plus a cloud VPC: HQ is the OSPF backbone and the single controlled egress to the cloud (IPsec + eBGP), so security policy is enforced in one place and remote areas only need a path to the hub.

rationale.subject: Site block BENGALURU
rationale.justification: Site subnets need 931 addresses in total; rounded up to one power-of-two block (/22, 1024 addresses) so the whole site can be advertised as a single summary route 10.50.16.0/22.

rationale.subject: Interior gateway protocol
rationale.justification: Design spans 4 geographically separate sites. Each remote site gets its own area (DELHI=Area 0, MUMBAI=Area 1, BENGALURU=Area 2, CHENNAI=Area 3) attached to backbone Area 0 at DELHI. This isolates routing domains: a flapping metro/WAN link only triggers SPF inside its own area, while other areas receive a single Type-3 summary LSA from the ABR. Combined with per-site summary blocks this keeps LSDB size and SPF cost bounded as sites grow.

rationale.subject: Route summarization
rationale.justification: Hierarchical VLSM gave every site one contiguous power-of-two block, so the ABR advertises exactly one summary per area instead of every VLAN. Summaries hide internal flaps from the rest of the network and shrink every routing table.

rationale.subject: Cloud boundary (AWS-VPC-MUMBAI)
rationale.justification: The cloud VPC is a separate administrative/routing domain; OSPF must not extend into a provider's network. eBGP gives policy control (prefix-lists, AS-path) and is what cloud VPN gateways speak natively. Only the enterprise aggregate is advertised (anchored with a Null0 route so it is always in the RIB), and only the VPC CIDR 10.100.0.0/16 is accepted. Private ASNs from RFC 6996 are used.

rationale.subject: DEL-BOM-WAN
rationale.justification: At 1400 km no un-amplified 10G single-mode optic closes the power budget (10G-ZR tops out at 80 km), and private dark fiber with DWDM amplification is not cost-justified. A carrier circuit is used, with a short OS2 1000BASE-LX SFP handoff at the carrier NID. Expected one-way delay ~8.918 ms (fiber route x1.3).

rationale.subject: DEL-BLR-WAN
rationale.justification: At 2150 km no un-amplified 10G single-mode optic closes the power budget (10G-ZR tops out at 80 km), and private dark fiber with DWDM amplification is not cost-justified. A carrier circuit is used, with a short OS2 1000BASE-LX SFP handoff at the carrier NID. Expected one-way delay ~13.696 ms (fiber route x1.3).

rationale.subject: DEL-MAA-WAN
rationale.justification: At 2200 km no un-amplified 10G single-mode optic closes the power budget (10G-ZR tops out at 80 km), and private dark fiber with DWDM amplification is not cost-justified. rationale.subject: Cloud VPN
rationale.decision: IKEv2 + IPsec VTI (AES-256, SHA-256, DH14, PFS)
rationale.justification: Traffic to AWS-VPC-MUMBAI crosses the public Internet, so it is encrypted in an IPsec tunnel. A route-based VTI (instead of a crypto-map) lets eBGP run over the tunnel and fail over dynamically. TCP MSS is clamped to 1379 bytes so ESP + outer-IP tunnel overhead never fragments 1500-byte packets.

rationale.subject: ACL IOT-SEGMENT
rationale.justification: Applied inbound on the VLAN 30 gateway interface, i.e. it filters traffic sourced from hosts in that VLAN. 6 entries, most specific first, ending in an explicit deny so denied flows are logged. Wildcard masks are computed bitwise from each subnet prefix (wildcard = ~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF).
